purpose: Create a falsifiable prior-art/originality research queue for Project-Frankenstein/EntityOS/HCU mechanisms after native functional reconstruction. This artifact MUST NOT be read as a novelty, patentability, first-in-world, consciousness or independent-invention finding.
epistemic_law: historical project source != proof of creation date unless Git supports the date
independent invention claim requires evidence of the project's chronology and the external chronology
patent novelty/nonobviousness are legal determinations outside this research artifact
native mechanism must be reconstructed before conventional labels are allowed to collapse distinctions

assessment_scale.NOT_ASSESSED: Candidate requires targeted prior-art search after native mechanism reconstruction.
assessment_scale.KNOWN_BROAD_PRIOR_ART_FAMILY: A broad related architecture/method family clearly predates the project; exact mechanism/combination overlap remains unassessed.
assessment_scale.LIKELY_NON_NOVEL_AT_BROAD_LEVEL: The broad proposition is strongly represented in prior literature; only narrower implementation details could remain distinct.
assessment_scale.POTENTIALLY_DISTINCT_COMBINATION_REQUIRE: Some elements are individually known but the exact project combination/causal contract has not been mapped.
assessment_scale.BLOCKED_NATIVE_HISTORY_INCOMPLETE: Do not assess originality before the project's own mechanism and first verified Git appearance are reconstructed.

external_primary_baseline.citation: Erman, Hayes-Roth, Lesser, Reddy. The Hearsay-II Speech-Understanding System: Integrating Knowledge to Resolve Uncertainty. ACM Computing Surveys 12(2), 1980. DOI 10.1145/356810.356816.
external_primary_baseline.relevance: Independent knowledge sources coordinate through a shared global blackboard/database containing hypotheses; strong broad prior art for shared-state cooperative problem solving and scheduling.

external_primary_baseline.citation: Barbara Hayes-Roth. A Blackboard Architecture for Control. Artificial Intelligence 26(3), 1985. DOI 10.1016/0004-3702(85)90063-3.
external_primary_baseline.relevance: Broad prior art for using a blackboard architecture to choose among potential actions and reason about/control problem-solving behavior.

external_primary_baseline.citation: Yao et al. ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models. arXiv:2210.03629 / ICLR 2023.
external_primary_baseline.relevance: Interleaves reasoning, actions and observations; broad prior art for closed language-agent reason/action loops.

external_primary_baseline.citation: Shinn et al. Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning. arXiv:2303.11366, 2023.
external_primary_baseline.relevance: Reflection over feedback stored in episodic memory to alter later decisions; broad prior art for reflection-memory-behavior loops.

external_primary_baseline.citation: Park et al. Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior. arXiv:2304.03442, 2023.
external_primary_baseline.relevance: Observation, long-term memory, reflection and planning architecture with ablations; broad prior art for persistent memory/reflection/planning agent loops.

external_primary_baseline.citation: Packer et al. MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems. arXiv:2310.08560, 2023.
external_primary_baseline.relevance: Virtual context management, multiple memory tiers and interrupts; broad prior art for externalized persistent memory/context management around LLMs.

external_primary_baseline.citation: Wang et al. Mixture-of-Agents Enhances Large Language Model Capabilities. arXiv:2406.04692, 2024.
external_primary_baseline.relevance: Layered multi-model aggregation; broad prior art for using multiple model instances/agents to improve model outputs, but not automatically for variable-N shared-state cognitive simulation.

external_primary_baseline.citation: Zou et al. Steering Language Models With Activation Engineering. arXiv:2308.10248, 2023.
external_primary_baseline.relevance: Inference-time activation interventions alter model behavior; broad prior art for activation/vector steering where an actual activation interface exists.

external_primary_baseline.citation: Cogitate Consortium et al. Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness. Nature 642, 133-142, 2025. DOI 10.1038/s41586-025-08888-1.
external_primary_baseline.relevance: Not software prior art for the project, but strong methodological prior art for preregistered divergent predictions and adversarial theory testing around GNWT.

queue.native_mechanism: Relevance appears when independently stored evidence dimensions overlap at query time: semantic similarity, time, provenance, causal lineage, current state, goals, perception, effects and confidence; ambiguous/unbound resolution fails closed and graph expansion remains a rebuildable projection.
queue.why_not_higher: Multi-signal and graph-assisted retrieval are broad mature families; current distinctness, if any, is more likely in the exact typed fail-closed authority/provenance contract than in the idea of combining relevance signals.

queue.prohibited_claim: Do not call Emergent Retrieval novel, world-first or patentable from current evidence.

required_next_method: For each priority item, reconstruct the native mechanism and first verified accessible Git appearance before broad web categorization.
Build element-by-element claim charts against primary papers/repos/patents where relevant; do not compare slogans.
Separate broad-family anticipation from narrower combination/implementation overlap.
Search backward from the project's first verified Git appearance; record publication/priority dates exactly.
Preserve negative matches and near-misses rather than optimizing toward novelty.
If patentability matters, hand the evidence chart to qualified legal review rather than converting engineering confidence into a legal opinion.
open_gap: This queue is intentionally conservative. The native Project-Frankenstein chronology remains incomplete, and the external search performed for this curation pass is a seed set, not an exhaustive patent/literature search.
